milestone.title: [tests] Convert pure-logic integration tests to in-process library calls

intent.outcome: After this ships, at least 60% of the 2140 `mp` subprocess spawns in `crates/mp/tests/` are replaced by direct `mp::...` library calls in a new `tests/common/lib_api.rs` helper. Test wall-clock drops proportionally; spec for the subprocess-required boundary is written and reviewed.

problem.description: `crates/mp/tests/common/mod.rs:218` `TestEnv::run` spawns the `mp` binary via `Command::new(mp_bin())` for every test step. With 2140 spawn sites across the integration tests, even at 50 ms average per spawn that is ~107 s of pure subprocess overhead per full `make test` run. Many of these calls exercise pure logic (validate, fragment read/write, projection, JSON shape assertions) that does not need a subprocess — they only need the test to verify the public lib API of `mp`.

in_scope: Spec: produce a 1-page 'test taxonomy' doc in `docs/concepts/03 - Testing/test-taxonomy.md` defining which categories must remain subprocess (install/uninstall, TUI, real-fs writes, end-to-end smoke) vs which can be in-process (validate, fragment ops, projection, store I/O on a TempDir, JSON parsing).
Add `crates/mp/tests/common/lib_api.rs` exposing the in-process surface (typed wrappers around `mp::validate`, `mp::fragment_*`, `mp::projection::*`, `mp::store::...`).

Convert at least the top 5 most-spawned test suites: `suite_validate`, `suite_fragment`, `suite_milestone`, `suite_step`, `suite_plan`. Each conversion keeps the existing assertions; only the spawn→call path changes.
Add `lib_api` benchmarks/tests that assert identical results between in-process and subprocess paths for the same inputs (parity guard).
out_of_scope: No change to `install`/`uninstall`/`doctor` test suites (real-fs, must remain subprocess).
No change to `watch_*` test suites (process supervision, must remain subprocess).
No new public API on `mp` — reuse existing pub functions.
M163 (server-mode socket tests) — separate, deferred (see idea ID-01).

findings.description: AC-04 quantitative threshold (≥20% cold make test drop) not met: actual 3-run mean delta is -1.96s (~2.1% drop). The spec's cost model assumed ~50ms per subprocess spawn; actual per-spawn time on this Mac is closer to ~1ms because cargo nextest's process-per-test architecture + the M132 mp_bin snapshot retry amortize the mp-bin cold-start. Converting all 392 top-5-suite spawn sites in-process would save ~400ms ≈ 0.4%, well below the 20% target. Verdict: spec-gap (analogous to M159 F-01, M160 F-01, M161 F-04). Recorded in mp-dogfood-log.md Entry 28 + AC-04 evidence. Closure path: re-spec AC-04 to a code-clarity metric (e.g. 'X% of top-5 suite assertions reachable via lib_api') since wall-clock isn't where the in-process conversion pays for itself.

findings.description: lib_api in-process wrappers return different JSON shapes than the CLI subprocess path in 4 places: (a) spec_status — in-process returns null, CLI returns ""; (b) lifecycle_at — in-process skips CLI's RFC3339 timestamp; (c) milestone_create — in-process returns raw MilestoneFile, CLI applies gate logic to set spec_status='draft'; (d) milestone_approve — CLI requires spec_status='draft' first (gated), in-process doesn't. The parity test (lib_api_parity.rs) deliberately compares only fields whose shape agrees. Closure path: either (1) update lib_api to apply the CLI's post-processing (more code, but exact parity), or (2) accept the shape drift as documented and let tests assert on the union of fields. Tracked in mp-dogfood-log.md Entry 28.
findings.fixed_in: wontfix (accepted shape-drift): chose path (2) from the F-03 closure-options — accept the documented shape drift between lib_api in-process wrappers and the CLI subprocess path, rather than replicate the CLI's post-processing in lib_api. The drift is real but bounded: (a) milestone_create — CLI wraps in {ok: true, milestone: summary}, in-process returns the full MilestoneFile; (b) milestone_approve — CLI gates via validate_milestone_ready + check_g14_approval_requests + plan_verify_ac, in-process calls apply_spec_status which only flips lifecycle+spec_status+execution_status; (c) milestone_complete — CLI also runs the G15 open-self-findings gate (which in-process DOES call), but lacks CLI's emit_gate_failure wrapper. The parity test (lib_api_parity.rs) deliberately compares only fields whose shape agrees (id, title, status, verification, evidence for AC fragments; errors/warnings arrays for validate; the same-field-presence check for milestone_create), avoiding the drift fields. The lib_api.rs module docs already document this contract in the doc-comment at the top of the file. Closure path: if any converted test later needs an exact-shape match (rare — the 7 converted validate_drift tests only assert on fields that agree), add a thin lib_api wrapper that calls the CLI-emit path. Time-box: out of scope for M162's pilot scope. Ext-reviewer concurs with the accept-drift choice.

findings.description: lib_api_parity.rs: milestone_ac_list_parity_14 is actually 15 assertions, not 14 — the trailing assertion (sub_arr[i]["verification"].as_str().is_some()) executes twice inside the for-i-in-0..2 loop (i=0 and i=1) but the trailing comment reads "// 14" without "// 14, 15". The runner's evidence text claims 52 byte-identical assertions across 4 tests; actual count is 53 (12+12+14+15). Either rename the test to milestone_ac_list_parity_15 and update the comment to "// 14, 15" (so the count and assertion numbering match), or drop one assertion to bring it back to 14. findings.description:
crates/mp/tests/common/lib_api.rs:25-28 states:

  "All functions take either a &PlanContext (preferred — explicit
  project_root + plan_dir) or a &Path (auto-derives a PlanContext
  via discover). Return types mirror the CLI's stdout:
  Result<serde_json::Value> for read-only commands, Result<()> for
  mutators that don't return a fragment."

Two claims are false:
1. **No function takes &Path.** The four `ctx_for*` helpers do, but
   they return `Result<PlanContext>`, not the result of a command.
   Every public command wrapper (validate, milestone_ac_show/list/pass/
   update_description, step_show, step_list, show_milestone,
   milestone_create/approve/complete) takes &PlanContext only.
2. **No mutator returns Result<()>** — every mutator returns
   `Result<Value>` (e.g. milestone_create, milestone_approve,
   milestone_complete, milestone_ac_pass,
   milestone_ac_update_description). The “Result<()> for mutators
   that don’t return a fragment” sentence is a leftover from a design
   that never shipped.

Fix: rewrite the Surface section to say “All wrappers take
&PlanContext. Helpers (ctx_for, ctx_for_env, ctx_for_workspace) build
a PlanContext from common inputs. All wrappers return
Result<serde_json::Value>.” (One-liner; doc-only.)
findings.summary: lib_api.rs doc-string claim is wrong: no function returns Result<()>, and ctx_for never auto-derives via discover

findings.description:
docs/concepts/03 - Testing/test-taxonomy.md:67-82 ("Category B — CAN
be in-process") lists these `mp::…` modules as the in-process API:

  - `mp::validate::run(ctx, project_root)` — actual: mp::validate::validate_plan
    (correct in spirit, API name drift).
  - `mp::milestone::criterion_show / criterion_list(ctx, id, ac_id)`
    — actual: ✅ wrapped in lib_api.
  - `mp::milestone::criterion_pass / criterion_update(...)` — ✅ wrapped.
  - `mp::projection::project_*(ctx, id, fragment)` — actual: NO WRAPPER
    in lib_api.rs.
  - `mp::step::load_*`, `mp::milestone::wp::load_*` — actual: ONLY
    step_show is wrapped (no wp wrappers, no other load_* wrappers).
  - `mp::plan_io::load(ctx, path)` — actual: NO WRAPPER in lib_api.rs.

So three rows of the in-process table claim APIs that aren't wrapped.
A contributor who reads the doc and tries to call lib_api::projection_xxx
will get a compile error ("no function or associated item named
`projection_xxx` found…"). Same for plan_io and wp.

The conversion recipe (lines 88-119) and the narrative above the table
are fine. Only the table itself overclaims.

Fix: trim Category B to the wrappers that actually exist
(`validate`, `milestone_ac_show/list/pass/update_description`,
`step_show`, `show_milestone`, `milestone_create/approve/complete`),
or add the missing wrappers. Recommended: trim the table; add the
wrappers in the M162 follow-up milestone alongside the 385 remaining
spawn-site conversions.
findings.summary: test-taxonomy.md lists mp::projection::*, mp::plan_io::load, mp::step::load_*, mp::milestone::wp::load_* as the in-process surface — only some of those are actually wrapped in lib_api.rs

findings.description:
crates/mp/tests/common/lib_api.rs:174-188 wraps `step_list` by
calling `mp::milestone::load_milestone_by_id(ctx, milestone_id)` and
projecting `m.steps` via `serde_json::to_value`. The doc-comment
explicitly acknowledges (lines 175-184): “the `mp::step` module does
not expose a dedicated list fn yet (M162 left as a follow-up)…
loading the milestone and projecting the steps field is byte-identical
to the CLI's `step show` output.”

But — the parity assertion that supposedly proves this is NOT in
lib_api_parity.rs. The parity test file only has 4 tests:
validate_parity_12, milestone_create_parity_12,
milestone_ac_show_parity_14, milestone_ac_list_parity_15. No
step_list parity.

So step_list ships an unverified “byte-identical” claim. If
`mp::model::Step` ever gains a `#[serde(skip)]` field that the CLI
projection strips (or vice versa), the in-process wrapper will
silently diverge from `mp step show <mid>`.

Other lib_api surface elements with similar characteristics
(step_show, criterion_show, criterion_list) have parity tests; only
step_list is uncovered.

Fix: add a `step_list_parity_NN` test mirroring the existing
milestone_ac_list_parity_15 shape — same fixture, lib_api::step_list
on one env + env.run(&["step", "show", &id]) on the second, assert
the JSON arrays match field-for-field on the Step fields that the
docstring assumes are byte-identical. (Id is auto-generated, so use
ordering.)

Severity is low because the projection is straight-forward and the
risk is low today, but the parity guard should be symmetric — every
wrapper that ships a “byte-identical” claim deserves a parity test.
findings.summary: lib_api::step_list has no parity assertion; lib_api_parity.rs only covers validate + 3 milestone_* tests

findings.description:
crates/mp/tests/lib_api_parity.rs declares 4 parity tests with
53 byte-identical assertions (12 + 12 + 14 + 15). AC-03 promises:

  "Parity guard: for at least 50 sample assertions across the 5
  converted suites, in-process and subprocess paths produce
  byte-identical stdout/stderr/exit-code [for the same inputs]."

Only ONE of the four tests satisfies "same inputs":

* validate_parity_12 (line 30-131): ONE TestEnv (env), then
  lib_api::validate(&ctx) AND env.run(&["validate",...]) against
  the same fixture. True parity.
* milestone_create_parity_12 (line 137-194): TWO TestEnvs
  (env and env2); each path runs on its own freshly-init'd TempDir.
  The assertions check "both paths return a milestone with
  title=Parity Test and non-empty id" — schema agreement, not
  byte-identical output of the same milestone. (Also many redundant
  assertions: 7 of 12 are 3 different ways to spell the same
  title check.)
* milestone_ac_show_parity_14 (line 234-276): same pattern,
  two envs, two independently-created milestones.
* milestone_ac_list_parity_15 (line 282-312): same pattern.

So 41 of the 53 assertions are schema-agreement on independent
fixtures, not byte-identity on the same fixture. A divergence where
the in-process wrapper reads from a different on-disk location
than the subprocess path (e.g., a context-derivation bug) would not
be caught by the AC/* tests. AC-03 evidence text claims "52
byte-identical assertions" — that's only true in a "schema agrees"
sense, not in a "same input" sense.

Fix options:
1. Make AC tests truly same-input: one env, in-process create-then-
   show, then subprocess show (read-only) of the same id. Bit-identical
   guaranteed because the in-process path wrote the file.
2. Or accept the weaker guarantee and downgrade the AC-03 spec to
   "schema agreement, plus a same-fixture test for each wrapper".
   Add the missing step_list parity test (see F-09).

Recommended: option 1 — restructure the create/AC parity tests to use
one env for state setup and exercise both read paths against the
same fixture; keep validate parity as the strongest test. Provides
real drift detection with no extra code beyond what's already there.
Either way, AC-03 text in 162-*.json should match the implementation.
findings.summary: milestone_create/ac_show/ac_list parity tests use independent fixtures, not same-input — only validate_parity is a true same-input test
